design.order: Three complete traversals of first arm then three of second arm; first arm alternates by pair. Estimators persist across all four pairs.
design.warmupRule: First three calls (1496–1498) of every traversal excluded only from warmed summaries; all original observations retained.
design.sourceTiming: Input source PTS/duration remain original exact rationals. Existing VT request timestamps still use frame indices/60; no timing or algorithm change.
design.workingBufferPolicy: Attributed current buffer readback occurs outside its timed call. Twelve first logical CPU copies retained, then saved only after all 288 timed calls, before 12 independent existing-primitive controls.

inventory.domain: Source-size bounded encoded sRGB proxy exported by NativeHDRProcessor. No new decode/conversion or model inference.
inventory.scope: Twelve consecutive natural source proxy frames1496…1507 for an isolated actual NativeOpticalFlow comparison. Repeated traversals introduce explicitly recorded1507→1496 index discontinuities; timings are not source-rate playback.

statisticsDefinition.median: middle value or mean of middle two
statisticsDefinition.stageFraction: 100*sum(stage)/sum(attributed outer wall in the same slice). Null stages omitted from stage distributions and never entered as zero observations. Denominator includes all selected outer calls.
statisticsDefinition.nestedPackGPU: Reported separately; already overlaps pack wall and is excluded from wall partition sums/fractions.
statisticsDefinition.residual: Exact recorded floating subtraction outer wall minus left-associated four stage sum. Signed and unclamped; independently replayed from stage boundaries.
statisticsDefinition.outerDelta: Attributed minus production, or 100*delta/production. Combined instrumentation/readback/module conditions, not isolated overhead or optimization.

timingSemantics.ciResizeReturnWallSeconds: Legacy CIContext CVPixelBuffer render returns after completion; includes actor hop, image/colour transforms, allocation and render wait, not isolated CI GPU time
timingSemantics.initialFrame: Actual pack and resize measured; VT and motion stages are null because no prior frame exists
timingSemantics.motionAssessmentCompletedWallSeconds: MLXVideoMotion initialization including flow import, assessment, erosion, joint eval and scalar readback
timingSemantics.packCommandGPUSeconds: Nested existing Metal command GPU end minus start; never added to wall-stage sum
timingSemantics.packCompletedWallSeconds: Existing halfWriter.write including actor hop, pool acquisition, Metal submission and awaited command completion
timingSemantics.prepareCompletedWallSeconds: Same external call boundary in both arms, including actor scheduling and completed prepare return
timingSemantics.residualWallSeconds: External total minus four available stage walls, signed and unclamped; nested pack GPU time excluded
timingSemantics.vtCallbackCompletionWallSeconds: Session.process wall including destination allocation, parameters, processing-completion callback and continuation scheduling; not isolated VT GPU time

applePrimaryReference.title: WWDC 2017 Session510: Advances in Core Image: Filters, Metal, Vision, and More
applePrimaryReference.paraphrase: The legacy CIContext rendering APIs for IOSurface/CVPixelBuffer finish rendering before returning. The newly introduced CIRenderDestination APIs return after issuing work. NativeImageIO uses the former API.
applePrimaryReference.qualification: The installed legacy API header names the precise method but does not itself repeat this completion sentence; primary Apple presentation supplies the explicit contract. No private implementation or current GPU timestamp instrumentation was inspected.

stages.name: halfWriterCompletedOperationWall
stages.completion: The writer awaits its command-buffer completion handler before returning; producer owners remain captured until completion.
stages.scope: Allocation, binding, encoding, GPU completion and actor scheduling/resumption.
stages.nestedGPUInterval: Existing gpuDurationSeconds is command.gpuEndTime minus gpuStartTime after completion, null if unavailable/nonpositive. This is the pack-command interval only and is not added to operation wall totals.

stages.name: resizeCompletedOperationWall
stages.completion: Legacy CIContext.render(to:CVPixelBuffer,bounds:colorSpace:) completes rendering before returning under the Apple contract above.
stages.scope: CI graph/transform setup, destination allocation, input/output colour conversion, rendering/completion and actor scheduling. Not a pure resize-kernel or GPU-only duration.
stages.doNotChange: Do not replace with CIRenderDestination, add waitUntilCompleted, add a GPU fence or insert CPU readback to make timing appear completed. That would change the measured production path.

stages.name: videoToolboxCompletedOperationWall
stages.completion: The installed VTFrameProcessor.h callback contract states frame processing is complete; the wrapper awaits that callback.
stages.scope: Two output allocations, frame/parameter setup, VT processing, completion delivery and continuation resumption. No exposed VT kernel-only GPU duration.

stages.name: mlxMotionCompletedOperationWall
stages.completion: Initializer evals vectors, confidence and statistics, then reads scalar statistics and computes reset before return. MLX C++ eval waits for all passed outputs.
stages.scope: Imports, graph construction, kernels, reductions, synchronization and the existing scalar readback. Additional eval/readback is unnecessary.

firstFrame.policy: The initial frame performs writer and resize then returns nil because previous is absent. VT/motion stages must be absent/null and excluded from stage distributions, never inserted as zero-duration observations.

totalAndResidual.policy: Use identical outer call boundaries for production and attributed copies; sum only nonoverlapping operation wall segments. Record total minus stage sum as a signed residual, without clamping. It covers state handling, timer/recording overhead, scheduling not enclosed by a stage, and boundary differences.
caveats: The nested writer GPU interval overlaps writer wall and must never be added to the wall partition.
Timer instrumentation can perturb scheduling. Compare production and copy completed totals; no instrumentation-free stage measurements are claimed.
Keep wraps, random-access hints, reset and previous-buffer lifecycle unchanged.
Do not retain additional historical working buffers or perform hashes/readbacks inside timing boundaries; use separate bounded untimed controls.
A completed wall duration is not an isolated GPU kernel duration, compilation time, full-model contribution, Live throughput or physical presentation measurement.

allCallsCSV.encoding: Every sample leaf flattened with dot-separated keys; sequence added. Strings verbatim, other values JSON literals. Blank cell is absent; null cell is explicit null. All cells round-trip to original sample leaves.

independentAudit.publisherReconciliation: All 288 sample records, 144 comparisons, 12 working controls, 45 resource rows and aggregate stage/arm statistics match this publication exactly; all 54 independent pins reverified.
checks: all source identities / order / wrap / bits / nested monotonic clocks / arithmetic

limitations: Production wrapper is compiled in DLSSMedia; renamed attributed wrapper is compiled in XCTest. Total timing differences combine instrumentation, asymmetric untimed working-buffer readback/RAM retention and module conditions, not isolated clock overhead or optimization benefit.
No added synchronization in timed flow. Existing algorithm, conversions, allocations, revision, owners and reset policy retained.
Production working buffers are private. Untimed independent conversion controls use the same writer/resize primitives, not production-private pixel capture.
Direct working-buffer readback and all motion hash/byte checks occur outside timing but influence operating conditions.
The 1496–1507 subset repeats; wrap is a discontinuity, not continuous source-rate playback.
No model, decoder, player, physical timing, broad motion-quality, optimization, Live or M5 claim.

The production-arm warmed 31.34 ms is not a source regression comparison against the earlier 22.87 ms allocation experiment. Readback, retained working copies, executable/module placement and run conditions differ.
Stage wall fractions identify this run's dominant operations; they do not prove an available optimization or expected full-player speedup.
The firstWorking CPU copies total 49.8 MB; direct-reference motion snapshots can hold about 149.3 MB across a matched pair, outside timed calls.
Current production/private working surfaces are not directly inspected; post-timing primitive controls validate the same conversion functions independently.

reproduction.availability: Ignored local archives/inputs are referenced by hash; public CSV and JSON retain all scalar observations and exact provenance.
